summary: Iter-14 frontend-only delta ('Sign in' nav button + /login route) verified end-to-end via Playwright. All 6 core review flows pass structurally with ONE analytics-payload bug discovered: the signin_click event fires with properties.source='direct' (from attribution auto-merge) instead of the required 'top_nav' — root cause is the property-spread order in /app/frontend/src/lib/analytics.js line 59 (`{ ...properties, ...attr, variant }` — attr overrides caller). Same latent bug also affects the pre-existing waitlist_button_click({source:'top_nav'}) but was not noticed until now. Everything else works: (1) Landing top-right nav renders both [data-testid='nav-signin-btn'] (LogIn icon + 'Sign in' text) and [data-testid='nav-waitlist-btn'] at 1280px; (2) at 390px mobile, nav-signin-btn is correctly hidden (sm:hidden), nav-waitlist-btn remains visible; (3) clicking nav-signin-btn triggers /api/analytics/track POST with event='signin_click' AND window.location.href assignment to `https://auth.emergentagent.com/?redirect=https%3A%2F%2Fscript-to-video-382.preview.emergentagent.com%2Fauth%2Fcallback` (captured via context.route interception that aborts the external nav); (4) /login as anon briefly renders [data-testid='login-page'] with 'Redirecting to sign in…' text then redirects to the same emergent auth URL; (5) /login with admin session_token=test_admin_1784712404860 cookie routes via react-router to /dashboard (verified page.wait_for_url('**/dashboard**')) and does NOT hit emergent auth (0 auth URLs captured); (6) logged-in top nav correctly hides nav-signin-btn + nav-waitlist-btn (both count=0) and shows [data-testid='logout-btn'] + admin badge pill. Backend spot-check via curl on 10 endpoints — all return expected codes (formats 200, analytics/track 200, auth/session 405 on GET expected, admin/stats 401 anon / 200 admin, attribution-matrix 200, attribution-matrix.csv 200, sanity 200, sanity/untagged 200, waitlist POST 200, short/script-to-video-382 404 correctly). Waitlist regression: form submit succeeds, success screen shows 'You're on the list' style text with share CTAs (1 LinkedIn button + 3 copy/share buttons rendered). Console clean apart from expected third-party CORS noise from auth.emergentagent.com/demobackend during the aborted external nav (filtered).

integration_issues.issue: analytics.js track() spreads attribution AFTER caller properties, causing caller-supplied properties.source='top_nav' to be OVERWRITTEN by attribution.source (e.g. 'direct'). Captured payload for signin_click: {"event":"signin_click","properties":{"source":"direct","medium":null,"campaign":null,"referrer_host":null,"variant":"B"},...}. Expected properties.source='top_nav' per iter-14 spec. Same regression silently affects waitlist_button_click (Layout.jsx line 12) which also passes source:'top_nav'. Fix: reorder the spread in /app/frontend/src/lib/analytics.js:59 from `{ ...properties, ...attr, variant }` to `{ ...attr, ...properties, variant }` — OR rename attribution fields (attr_source/attr_medium) so they never collide with caller-provided property keys. Impact: any signin_click / waitlist_button_click analytics segment 'by source' will attribute all clicks to the visitor's traffic source (direct/twitter/…) instead of the nav-button surface — analytics for measuring which surface converted the user is currently broken.

action_items: FIX (HIGH): /app/frontend/src/lib/analytics.js line 57-62 — change `properties: { ...properties, ...attr, variant }` so attribution never overrides caller-supplied properties. Simplest patch: swap to `{ ...attr, ...properties, variant }` (caller wins). This restores properties.source='top_nav' for both signin_click and waitlist_button_click as spec'd in iter-14 and iter-12.

OPTIONAL (LOW): If preserving attribution alongside the caller's source is desired, rename the attribution keys (e.g. attr_source, attr_medium, attr_campaign, attr_referrer_host) so both dimensions coexist without collision.

OPTIONAL (LOW, carry-over): iter-13 already flagged that /admin?tab=experiments matrix footnote lacks data-testid and iter-12 flagged WaitlistForm.jsx lines 109/114 outline buttons inheriting text-white in dark bg — neither is iter-14 scope.
critical_code_review_comments: Layout.jsx (lines 44-55) — Fragment wrapping the two unauth buttons is correct; `hidden sm:inline-flex` on nav-signin-btn cleanly hides it below 640px (Tailwind sm breakpoint) while keeping nav-waitlist-btn always visible. LogIn icon import from lucide-react is imported at line 2. onClick order `track(...); login();` fires the analytics POST before the redirect kicks the tab away — since track() is fire-and-forget (returns a promise, no await) the fetch/xhr should be flushed to the browser network stack before the top-level nav completes. This matches how waitlist_button_click behaves. NOTE: If Chrome ever fails to send a beacon-style fetch on unload, we may lose signin_click events; consider using navigator.sendBeacon for these terminal actions.

Login.jsx — Correct guard: waits for `loading` to settle before deciding, redirects to /dashboard for authed users via react-router navigate({replace:true}), else fires login() from AuthCallback which sets window.location.href to the emergent auth URL. useEffect deps [user, loading, navigate] are correct. Renders a stable [data-testid='login-page'] with 'Redirecting to sign in…' — verified.

App.js — <Route path='/login'> is registered BEFORE the protected /dashboard route — correct so anon users don't get bounced by ProtectedRoute before Login gets a chance to render. The synchronous hash-check at the top of AppRouter (`if (location.hash?.includes('session_id='))` short-circuits routing to AuthCallback if the emergent redirect comes back to /login itself — subtle but correct.

AuthCallback.jsx login() (line 7-11) — Kept unchanged as noted in the review; still constructs redirectUrl from window.location.origin + '/auth/callback' and encodes it as the ?redirect= query param. Correctly does NOT hardcode any auth URL fallback.

analytics.js line 59 — BUG: `properties: { ...properties, ...attr, variant }` — attr is spread AFTER caller props, so any caller-supplied property that has the same key as an attribution field (source, medium, campaign, referrer_host) is silently overwritten. This defeats the iter-14 spec that says properties.source must be 'top_nav'. Empirical evidence in this test run: POST body captured `{..."source":"direct"...}`. Also affects waitlist_button_click, expo_click_share, etc. — likely all 'source' identifiers passed by callers are currently overwritten by attribution.

TopBar unauth branch — Buttons intentionally rendered as sibling <button>+<Button/> instead of grouping them into a shared container with matching heights; visually the 'Sign in' text-only link (h auto) is a bit shorter than the pill 'Join waitlist' (h-10) but both are vertically centered by the flex row — acceptable. Consider adding aria-label='Sign in' to the button for a11y since the inner text 'Sign in' + icon already reads correctly to screen readers.

rca of the issue: signin_click analytics missing source='top_nav' — RCA: /app/frontend/src/lib/analytics.js function track(event, properties={}) builds the POST body as `{ event, properties: { ...properties, ...attr, variant }, ... }`. Because JavaScript object-spread later keys OVERWRITE earlier keys, `attr = getAttribution() = { source, medium, campaign, referrer_host }` unconditionally clobbers the caller's `source: 'top_nav'` with e.g. `source: 'direct'` (or 'linkedin', 'twitter' depending on attribution). Repro: (1) open / as anon, (2) DevTools → Network → filter 'track', (3) click 'Sign in' in top nav, (4) inspect request body — you'll see properties.source='direct'. Mitigation: reorder to `{ ...attr, ...properties, variant }` — caller-supplied props win (small risk: if a caller passes a key that legitimately matches an attribution key it silently overrides attribution — but callers only pass 'source' intentionally so this is desired). Alternative mitigation: namespace attribution keys as attr_source, attr_medium, etc. so caller and attribution never collide. Choose #1 for minimum diff.
